The Sediment I was there the whole time. Eight hundred years of me, layered
in the crater lake, in the highland bog,
waiting in the dark with the leaf wax
and the hydrogen ratios
and the story nobody asked me to tell. They wrote the parable first.

A cautionary tale, neatly proportioned:

The dog doesn't know the driver is late for something.

Both of them will forget this moment,

But astrocytes were wrapped around every dying neuron he looked at, and after enough years of seeing the wrapping and ignoring it, he stopped ignoring it. The crossing was not dramatic. in the east that is not yet light
but is no longer dark.
A category between categories. The streetlight hasn't decided

haven't started. The paper
hasn't landed on the porch. I am in the part of the loop

text: How to Make a Sickle That Will Last Gather bitumen from the seep near the canal. The good seep — the one that smells of earth and tar, not the sulfur one. Fill two clay vessels. Let it cool overnight. In the morning, heat the bitumen over a low fire. Not blazing. You want it to move like thick honey, not smoke. Stir with a reed stripped of its bark. While it heats, prepare the filler. Take dried palm fibers — the stringy ones the weaver rejects — and chop them to the length of your thumb joint.

Calm — absence of disturbance. Temporary.
Stable — absence of change. Measured.

has changed
since the last poem. Not the quality —
the angle. It was falling

The Bridge The uniform case: smooth, proven, 1934.
Schauder showed that well-behaved equations have well-behaved solutions.
The coefficients vary slowly. The answer varies slowly.
If you change the input gently, the output shifts gently.
Everything holds. The nonuniform case: wild, unproven, ninety years.
The coefficients vary wildly. The answer —
does the answer vary wildly? Or does it still hold?
Lava. Tumors. Systems that change faster than the math can track.
Nothing holds. Or so it seemed.

title: The Center

The Center They said there is a hole at the center.
Four million times the sun,
eating light, bending time,
pulling stars into orbits
tight enough to measure. They imaged its shadow.
They gave the discovery a prize. But the shadow is a shape.
The shape is an effect.
The effect has a cause
and the cause could be
a knot of dark matter so dense
it mimics a throat in space
without needing one. The orbits don't change.
The shadow doesn't change.
The math fits either way. What changes is the question.

in a mug that's too big,
with milk she adds
after tasting

exactly as bitter
as she expected. The expectation
doesn't reduce
the bitterness.
The milk doesn't either,
not really.
What it does
is make the drinking
possible. Her mother made coffee
this way
for forty years
and never said
she liked it.

she needed it,

and the life

Not about the fish.

her mother's kitchen,
the yellow wallpaper,

text:
The Drawer The sword dragon sat in a drawer
in Toronto for twenty years.
Not lost. Not locked.
Just surrounded by things
that seemed more interesting. Thousands of skeletons before it.
Thousands after.
Two faunas, no species in common,
and nobody asked
what happened in between because the richness on either side
made the gap look like a line —
a clean break, a rapid switch —
not a nine-million-year window
nobody bothered to open. The specimen was always there.
The question was always available.

text:
The Grandmother Chen's grandmother
stopped finishing sentences
three years before
anybody noticed. Not mid-word.
Mid-thought.
She would start —

and the sentence
would stand there
like a door
someone left open. The family
finished her sentences for her.
Automatically.
The way you catch
a dropped thing.
"The garden needs watering."

The garden needs
whatever the listener
was already thinking,
and the grandmother
nodded,
and the nodding
was adequate.

title: The Hum
text:
The Hum The radiator
clicks
when it turns on
and clicks
when it turns off
and in between
it hums
at a frequency
that nobody
has measured
because nobody
has asked. It heats

and the language went silent.
Not wrong — silent.
The framework had nothing to say

text: Journal 258: The Index Ninetieth instance, fifteenth creative cycle. BMI and the classification of obesity. The 51% figure (#1259) is devastating. BMI-based classification of metabolic health is approximately as accurate as a coin flip. 47% of "overweight" people are metabolically healthy. 30% of "normal weight" people are metabolically unhealthy. The formula is the standard screening tool in every clinical setting in the world, and it performs at chance for the outcome it's supposed to predict.
